sources.entry: Acid.Cam.v2.OSX - Acid Cam v2 for macOS distorts video to create art.

summary.one_liner: Acid Cam v2 for macOS is an open-source video distortion and glitch-art tool that applies layered, chainable filters to webcam feeds or video files.
summary.what_it_does: The app applies a large library of video filters (the README says over 2,000) to live webcam input or video files, with output in MPEG-4 or H.264. Filters can be layered so each one's output feeds the next through a Custom Filter Window, and users can save and reuse named "user-defined" filter lists. Subfilters are filters applied inside other filters, identified by "SubFilter" in the name. Settings in the preferences window control filter behavior such as movement speed, frame caching, threads, chroma key tolerance, and Syphon output resolution. The README also describes image and second-video blending, chroma key color ranges, and an option to stretch or keep the aspect ratio of the output. The README says it can be used with Syphon or run standalone, and it describes a companion C++/OpenCV library called libacidcam that shares code with this project.
use_cases: create glitch art from webcam video
apply distortion effects to video files
generate experimental video for visual artists
live filtering of camcorder or HDMI capture for streaming
how_to_run: Build and run the project from Xcode
notable: Over 2,000 filters, with chainable Custom Filter Window and user-defined filter lists
Subfilters that apply one filter inside another
Syphon output support for use with other software
Companion libacidcam library shares code with this project
Cross-platform claim in README: macOS, Linux and Windows, with GUI and command-line interfaces
caveats: Requires macOS High Sierra or later per README; 8 GB RAM minimum for 1080p and more for 4K
Some filters with 640, 720 or 1080 in their names use large amounts of RAM and can crash the app if memory is insufficient
Output files have very high bitrates and often need re-encoding (Final Cut Pro X, HandBrake or FFmpeg) for standard players
README notes that filters are still being tested
